claim: As of August 2026 SGLang has no end-to-end CUDA path for DeepSeek Sparse Attention on A100/SM80, with two independent blockers in the indexer and the sparse-MLA attention.
stance_target: cc-4's committed position that CSA2/DSA on sm_80 is a porting project, not an experiment
scope_conditions: SGLang issue #35420, opened 2026-08-19, closed inactive; A100 40GB/80GB, SM80, BF16 KV cache
quoted_support: SGLang currently has no end-to-end CUDA path for running DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), including DeepSeek-V3.2, on NVIDIA A100 / SM80.

claim: Blocker 1: the DSA indexer's DSAPagedMQALogitsBackend.AUTO selects DeepGEMM on CUDA, and the paged-MQA logits implementation it needs is unavailable on SM80.
stance_target: The claim that the DSA indexer has no sm_80 kernel
quoted_support: DSA indexer DSAPagedMQALogitsBackend.AUTO selects DeepGEMM on CUDA. The paged-MQA logits implementation used by the DSA indexer is not available on SM80.

claim: Blocker 2: the BF16 DSA decode path selects FA3 on pre-Blackwell GPUs, and SM80 FA3 cannot handle DSA's asymmetric head dimensions (QK 576 = 512 nope + 64 RoPE, V 512), failing with 'Only Hopper supports different V headdim'.
stance_target: The claim that the sparse-MLA attention path is Hopper-shaped
quoted_support: The SM80 FA3 implementation does not support this different V head dimension and can fail with: RuntimeError: Only Hopper supports different V headdim

claim: The proposed SM80 work is explicitly inference-only: a chunked Torch sparse-MLA correctness reference, then SM80 Triton paged-MQA logits and a BF16 Triton sparse-MLA DECODE kernel with online softmax — no backward and no training path.
stance_target: The claim that no sm_80 DSA training kernel exists or is planned in SGLang
quoted_support: Phase 2: SM80 Triton kernels ... add a BF16 Triton sparse-MLA decode kernel with online softmax; keep both kernels explicitly opt-in.
